chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Leaving La Conga: Miami, Cuba, California

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So it must have been -- okay, I still want to get into some feelings, some memories of the days, the mid-to-late '40s. You know, when you -- did you -- you finished in 1946, playing at La Conga, and then began playing the jazz houses?

No, I left La Conga in 1945 in the month of December, went to Miami for the (unintelligible) festival and I played there, and I played a week there, two weeks before the New Year's Eve. And then they have -- two or three weeks, and then they had to change it. They bring in the ice show and they gave us a week rest, and I jumped to Cuba because I'd gotten to Havana January 1, 1946 on the first night I left Miami, right after I got through working.
And then I came back. And then when I'm closed in Miami, I came to New York. I played the Rio Cristada, was the name, maybe a month and a half. I went to the Club Racine in California.
Then I came back. Then after I got back
I started fooling around and that's when I started messing around with that jazz thing. And I started playing this.
